a.text: The first time I saw an Infected shatter was in the middle of a lake.
I was seven, young and innocent. It was my dream to become captain of the Miner's Patrol.
I'd get to stay up late at night, wear a cool uniform, and walk around with a bright torch.
Most families in Rim Billiton made their living in mining, digging, and processing ore. We did everything to prevent Infection.
But accidents happen.
One day, the adults came home early.
Mother and the other women of the house whispered in a corner. The men smoked in silence, until the entire room was filled with that acrid scent.
In between coughs, I ran around the living room, pretending to be a surveyor looking for new veins in a fog-filled valley.
Dad grabbed me by the collar and put me to bed.
I woke up earlier than usual the next day. I think I was trying to grab a can of soda while nobody was watching.
Grandma was sitting in the living room next to her luggage, She said she was going on a journey.
I pestered her to let me go with her. She could never say no to me. She said I could come a short way with her, then I had to go back home.
We saw a salt lake in the distance. It was a shallow one that only appeared in the rainy season, but it rained a lot that year. We couldn't see the other side of the lake.
Grandma told me that was as far as I could go. I said alright. She made me promise, like when she made me promise I would be a good boy when I first went to school.
But I wasn't a good boy anymore. I quietly followed her, hiding behind a bush when she got to the lakeside.
Grandma got onto a boat with a few people on it. They all had strange stones growing out of their bodies, and one of them was wrapped up in a blanket. The boatman turned on the engine.
I watched from the shore as the boat disappeared into the fog.
I was confused. Grandma didn't say anything to me on our way; it was like an ordinary picnic trip.
I was about to turn around, thinking about where I would have breakfast before going home, then I heard a sound like crystal shattering.
I turned around and saw Originium dust sprayed into the air, mixing with the fog, reflecting an eerie glow in the sun.
It was like a dream.

steps.name: Red
steps.text: Was that how you got infected?

steps.name: Guard
steps.text: No, I was lucky. That time.

steps.name: Guard
steps.text: Maybe it really was a dream, brought about by a summer morning.

steps.name: Guard
steps.text: But I never saw Grandma again, and my family never talked about her anymore.

steps.name: Red
steps.text: She...

steps.name: Guard
steps.text: She was always thoughtful and cautious. It wasn't like her to let a child follow her, putting him in danger.

steps.name: Guard
steps.text: For once, though, she made a selfish choice on her journey.

steps.name: Guard
steps.text: She wanted to spend just a little more time with her grandson. Maybe she even wanted to give me a hug.

steps.name: Guard
steps.text: Now I remember. I didn't even get to show her my report card that semester.

a.text: It was the best I ever did in school.
The sounds of the forest stopped. The flickering light shining through the shadows of the trees no longer moved.
Then, came the sound of lament and painful moaning.

steps.name: Guard
steps.text: On your guard, Red. The Victorians have stopped.

steps.name: Guard
steps.text: Looks like they're planning to make camp.

steps.name: Red
steps.text: Here? It's only a few hundred meters from our camp.

steps.name: Red
steps.text: They no longer have the strength to cover their tracks. Who knows if there's a scouting party shadowing them somewhere.

a.text: Red's hands never stop, even as he complains, cutting away the bothersome vines.
We approach their position and see their flickering shadows through the sparse bushes.
Soldiers lie on the ground in exhaustion, hopelessly burying their heads amongst the falling leaves. The sergeant sits down on a rock, silently polishing his sword, the only weapon he has left.

steps.name: Guard
steps.text: I guess they just didn't have the strength to go any further.

steps.name: Red
steps.text: These people don't have the luxury to think. They're still living in a dream.

steps.name: Guard
steps.text: 'It'll all pass.'

steps.name: Red
steps.text: Were they really just 'separated' from the rest of the army?

steps.name: Red
steps.text: These Victorians are lucky. They faced a gentle exile, not the swords of their comrades.

steps.name: Guard
steps.text: It's not easy to accept that you're Infected.

steps.name: Guard
steps.text: We should wait for them to understand who they are, and for them to make a choice.

steps.name: Red
steps.text: Do you really mean to take them in? These... 'soldiers'?

steps.name: Guard
steps.text: We're weak. So are they.

steps.name: Red
steps.text: What's the plan, then?

steps.name: Guard
steps.text: Finish the shift, and notify the sentries. Expand the patrols to include this camp.

steps.name: Guard
steps.text: The Infected stand together.

a.text: 'Stand Together.' Pretty words.
Of course we had to stand together. What other choice did we have?
But are the words 'stand together' so simple that we fail to appreciate their true meaning?
Oripathy changed all our lives equally, robbed us of our futures equally.
But is what is taken from a farmer who has to pay his taxes out of seeds stored for next year's planting equal to what is taken from a wealthy merchant with a safe full of pure gold?
When what we had to begin with was not equal, neither are the choices that survive deprivation.
Who are we really standing together with, then?

steps.name: Excited Infected
steps.text: You're Talulah, right?

steps.name: Nervous Infected
steps.text: Founder of the Reunion, leader of the Infected! They say you did great things in Ursus!

steps.name: Excited Infected
steps.text: All the Infected of Victoria are talking about you. Is it true that you captured a city?

steps.name: Nervous Infected
steps.text: A city for the Infected? Is it still there?

steps.name: Talulah
steps.text: I'm no leader. I'm just a member of the Reunion Movement.

steps.name: Talulah
steps.text: Have some porridge. We're setting out soon.

steps.name: Excited Infected
steps.text: Tell us more about your city, Talulah!

steps.name: Talulah
steps.text: It's...

steps.name: Excited Infected
steps.text: Oh, no need to hang your head! I suppose things didn't go so smoothly, if you're in Victoria now.

steps.name: Nervous Infected
steps.text: Of course the uninfected wouldn't let us win that easily, after trampling on us for so long.

steps.name: Excited Infected
steps.text: What does it matter if those scum tripped you up once? You're Reunion!

steps.name: Excited Infected
steps.text: We all believe in you!

a.text: Talulah looks down at the pot she is stirring, serving bowl after bowl of hot porridge.
The steam from the pot obscures her vision.

steps.name: Talulah
steps.text: Careful, it's hot.

steps.name: Reunion Soldier
steps.text: They all believe in you.

steps.name: Reunion Soldier
steps.text: What do you think about that, eh? Being the hope of so many?

steps.name: Nervous Infected
steps.text: You're a veteran from Ursus, aren't you? What are you talking about?

steps.name: Guard
steps.text: Valiya.

steps.name: Reunion Soldier
steps.text: I know... sorry, couldn't resist. Hmph.

steps.name: Excited Infected
steps.text: Is it true that there was a bit of trouble at the camp yesterday?

steps.name: Guard
steps.text: It's fine. All taken of.

steps.name: Guard
steps.text: Stop crowding Talulah like that and start packing. We have a long way to go today.

steps.name: Nervous Infected
steps.text: Oh yeah, I still have fertilizer to load onto the truck.

steps.name: Guard
steps.text: And it's not 'You Reunion' any more.

steps.name: Excited Infected
steps.text: Oh yeah, we're Reunion too. Haha!

steps.name: Excited Infected
steps.text: See you later.

steps.name: Talulah
steps.text: Guard...

steps.name: Guard
steps.text: It's fine. No need to say anything.

a.text: I take the bowl of porridge from Talulah. She's very pale.

steps.name: Guard
steps.text: There are things we can't tell them yet.

steps.name: Talulah
steps.text: I know. It's your decision.

steps.name: Guard
steps.text: Reunion can't collapse again.

steps.name: Talulah
steps.text: I'm the banner that you rally to in Victoria. I accept that.

steps.name: Talulah
steps.text: But I'm deceiving them. I'm still...

steps.name: Guard
steps.text: It's no more or less than you deserve.

steps.name: Guard
steps.text: It's none of my business whether you see this as an honor or punishment for your crimes. What the others need is hope.

steps.name: Guard
steps.text: Are you going to tell them you were under the influence of an evil god, and everything that happened at Chernobog was an Ursine plot?

steps.name: Guard
steps.text: I would rather our organization be built on a lie.

steps.name: Talulah
steps.text: We were built on a lie back then too.

steps.name: Guard
steps.text: I know. Payback will come, someday, but at least this time we lied for the Infected.

steps.name: Guard
steps.text: There are no second chances for Reunion. I hope we don't go down the same path you did.

steps.name: Guard
steps.text: What did that sister of yours say in Chernobog?

steps.name: Guard
steps.text: 'Until the day when the Infected are judged fairly.'

steps.name: Talulah
steps.text: I'll wait.

steps.name: Talulah
steps.text: I'll be your tool until that day comes.

steps.name: Injured Soldier
steps.text: Er, excuse me...

steps.name: Guard
steps.text: What are you doing here, Victorian?

steps.name: Injured Soldier
steps.text: I'm not armed. Your sentries searched me.

steps.name: Injured Soldier
steps.text: I... I caught a whiff. My brothers haven't eaten in four days. Some of them... I don't know, they don't look good.

steps.name: Injured Soldier
steps.text: I have a lighter here, and... d-do you want brass buttons? If you could be so kind as to trade some bread for these...

steps.name: Injured Soldier
steps.text: I-I know, it's not enough... I have a bunch of good leather back at my home in Blackstream! Once I get back, I'll sell it and pay you back double!

a.text: The young man gazes hungrily at the pot, his hand grabbing his own uniform tightly, perhaps out of nervousness, or trying to straighten it out to look more presentable.
Talulah puts a bowl of porridge before him.

steps.name: Talulah
steps.text: You can take what's left in the pot.

steps.name: Injured Soldier
steps.text: Th-Thank you! Here's the lighter. Sometimes you need to click it a few times before it lights. And the button—

a.text: I take the lighter and grab the hand trying to rip the buttons off.

steps.name: Guard
steps.text: It's fine. Eat.

a.text: He practically pours the food down his throat.

steps.name: Guard
steps.text: Where's your sergeant?

steps.name: Injured Soldier
steps.text: I don't know. We haven't seen him all morning. I was worried he would barge into your camp again.

steps.name: Injured Soldier
steps.text: Say, did you hear any sounds in the night? Like artillery fire?

steps.name: Guard
steps.text: No reports of anything like that.

steps.name: Injured Soldier
steps.text: He... never mind. Everyone's gone mad. Us, them, there's no sane man left on the front.

steps.name: Guard
steps.text: Sound like things are rough out there.

steps.name: Injured Soldier
steps.text: Rough, eh...? You have no idea what the Sarkaz are using against us.

steps.name: Injured Soldier
steps.text: They have no battleships, no armored vehicles. We thought the devils were just barbarians, fighting our armies with swords and bows.

steps.name: Injured Soldier
steps.text: How wrong we were. Could you imagine an entire squad of Sarkaz casters, casting their Arts at the same time?

steps.name: Injured Soldier
steps.text: It was more terrifying than any artillery or ballista fire. Get hit by a shell, and you might lose an arm or leg, the fragments digging themselves into your flesh, causing terrible pain.

steps.name: Injured Soldier
steps.text: But the Sarkaz, they turned the battlefield to the Hell of Lateran tales.

steps.name: Injured Soldier
steps.text: I saw armored vehicles pierced by lightning bolts of blood, my mates melted into puddles of gore...

steps.name: Injured Soldier
steps.text: I never imagined it would turn out like this when the Duke of Fife's men dragged me out of the cystybeast pens—

steps.name: Injured Soldier
steps.text: Forget it. I'd rather not think about anything. Thanks for the porridge. I'll bring the pot back later.

steps.name: Talulah
steps.text: You can keep it. We have plenty of them, and it might be of use to you.

steps.name: Injured Soldier
steps.text: Thank you so much. I'll never forget it. Are you leaving? Where are you going?

steps.name: Injured Soldier
steps.text: This is pretty much a battlefield now, and it's Victorian lands all around... for the Infected...

steps.name: Injured Soldier
steps.text: Oh, I'm sorry, I shouldn't have asked. Forget I said anything.

a.text: The soldier hurries to leave, grabbing the side of the pot with his one good hand and supporting the bottom with the limp arm, grimacing at the heat.
I reach into my pocket and dig out what I just got from the doctor.

steps.name: Guard
steps.text: Hey, wait!

a.text: I go up to him and put the vial of medicine in his pocket.

steps.name: Injured Soldier
steps.text: What's this?

steps.name: Guard
steps.text: It'll relieve some of the worst symptoms. You can share it with the others.

steps.name: Guard
steps.text: I'll visit Blackstream and collect what you owe me.

steps.name: Injured Soldier
steps.text: I—sir...

steps.name: Guard
steps.text: Go.

steps.name: Injured Soldier
steps.text: ...You'll love our village.

steps.name: Injured Soldier
steps.text: Thanks.

steps.name: Talulah
steps.text: You really are like the Rhodes Islanders.

steps.name: Talulah
steps.text: I heard you were the one who found the doctors who knew how to make the medicine.

steps.name: Guard
steps.text: To be honest, what we're making hardly even qualifies as medicine compared to the suppressants that I knew.

steps.name: Guard
steps.text: Rhodes Island offers low-cost treatment plans, but at the end of the day, they're a company. They need research funding, and they have corporate due diligence to deal with.

steps.name: Guard
steps.text: Who knows how many eyes are on them in Kazimierz and Columbia?

steps.name: Talulah
steps.text: That's why you persuaded Nine to go north. The warriors say there's a factory there.

steps.name: Guard
steps.text: A tiny pharmaceutical factory.

steps.name: Guard
steps.text: So small it's barely even a workshop. It's not even on a nomadic plate, but that one little piece of land was once the salvation of many Infected.

steps.name: Guard
steps.text: That, is, until it grew big enough that it caught people's attention. Some of the ones driven out of there joined us, and that's how we heard the story.

steps.name: Guard
steps.text: It's deep in the forest, where nobody's watching. We need medicine, even if it's just a pale imitation of the real thing. But more importantly—

steps.name: Guard
steps.text: —It was once a starting point of Victoria's Reunion Movement.

steps.name: Guard
steps.text: We have to unite those scattered across Victoria. We have to tell them that help has come.

steps.name: Guard
steps.text: I've seen plenty of Infected self-help organizations. Kind souls helped us from time to time, but in the end, none of them lasted.

steps.name: Guard
steps.text: When I was at Rhodes Island, I often wondered if things would get better if everyone worked harder and made more medicine.

steps.name: Guard
steps.text: Maybe. But Chernobog changed my mind.

steps.name: Guard
steps.text: Why do they crack down on workshops like these? Why are kindness and hard work warped by hatred and prejudice?

steps.name: Guard
steps.text: When evil itself is fuzzy as the fog, why does everyone, even the Infected themselves, decide to wait for their own deaths in the middle of a lake?

a.text: I stare at Talulah, who hardly reacts to my words. Her eyes are calm, unusually so.
Her soul is too weary, having seen too much. What has become of the woman who was once our leader?
Or had she uttered the same words before, and seen what came of them?

steps.name: Guard
steps.text: *sigh*... You know what I mean.

steps.name: Guard
steps.text: Oripathy is an illness, but... we'll leave the illnesses to Rhodes Island, for now.

steps.name: Guard
steps.text: Our enemy isn't just Oripathy; it's oppression and prejudice, the truths they've tried to cover up with Oripathy.

steps.name: Guard
steps.text: Oripathy is just the culmination of all the decay across the lands.

steps.name: Guard
steps.text: Taking back a symbol may help the Infected of Victoria realize that and stand together with us.

steps.name: Talulah
steps.text: ...Stand together.

steps.name: Guard
steps.text: That's something only Reunion can do.

steps.name: Talulah
steps.text: Have you told the others how you think?

steps.name: Guard
steps.text: Hm? Of course. I'm always talking to Nine about our—

steps.name: Talulah
steps.text: No. You know the one I'm talking about.

steps.name: Guard
steps.text: Oh...

steps.name: Guard
steps.text: A little. I got a... gentle answer. That's why I'm here.

steps.name: Guard
steps.text: Whatever the case, we didn't choose the same path, so I... er...

steps.name: Guard
steps.text: It's not my place to ask for more.

a.text: Of course it isn't.
Rhodes Island is a paradise of idealists. Me? A man who could only see what stands right in front of me.
The gain and loss right in front of me...
I heard the veteran guerilla fighters talk about the old days of the Reunion in the tundra, the ideals that everyone held.
'A city of the Infected, our home.'
Some of them thought it was just within reach. It was almost realized at Chernobog, but fell short in the end.
But I know the city of our dreams is still far, far away.
And how could a single city be enough?
What could a single city do?

steps.name: Percival
steps.text: You're still limping. Maybe you should go sit in the back?

steps.name: Guard
steps.text: Just a little sprain.

steps.name: Percival
steps.text: You haven't been on a lot of expeditions lately.

steps.name: Guard
steps.text: My squad passed through the wilderness the other day with Infected comrades from Greewich.

steps.name: Guard
steps.text: The earth had been torn open, with ditches everywhere. Looked like one of the turnip farms back home, except much smaller.

steps.name: Guard
steps.text: I tripped.

steps.name: Percival
steps.text: *snort*

steps.name: Percival
steps.text: What was it? I didn't think there a place like that near Londinium.

steps.name: Guard
steps.text: Walt said that all those trenches, hundreds of them, each one big enough to fit our entire squad, were battleship tread marks.

steps.name: Percival
steps.text: No wonder you've looked worried.

steps.name: Percival
steps.text: It takes all my strength just to go from day to day.

steps.name: Percival
steps.text: Don't think too much about it.

steps.name: Reunion Member
steps.text: A report from the scouts, Guard.

steps.name: Reunion Member
steps.text: We heard sounds from the woods on the left side up ahead.

steps.name: Reunion Member
steps.text: The Originium zone sensor went off when we got closed, so we couldn't be sure exactly what it was.

steps.name: Guard
steps.text: Send word to the rest of the team. We'll go around.

steps.name: Reunion Member
steps.text: Roger.

steps.name: Guard
steps.text: Percival.

steps.name: Percival
steps.text: I'll come along with a few guys. Don't want you to trip again.

a.text: There's an unsettling smell in the air.
The instruments show a high level of Active Originium. Not a good sign.

steps.name: Guard
steps.text: Remember your protective measures. Keep your masks on.

a.text: Was that a man under the tree?
No, it's a Victorian uniform, ripped almost beyond recognition, but somehow familiar. A sergeant's badge lies on the ground next to it.
A tiny music box sits a short distance away, covered in Originium dust, but still barely playing.

steps.name: Guard
steps.text: ...Infected confirmed dead. We should leave.

a.text: Percival walks slowly, humming along with the scattered music.

steps.name: Percival
steps.text: Do you know this song, Guard?

steps.name: Guard
steps.text: No, but I've heard it before.

steps.name: Percival
steps.text: ...The sun on the meadow is summery warm♪♫Filling our home with euphoria♬♪

steps.name: Percival
steps.text: We gather together to greet the storm♪♫Tomorrow belongs to Victoria♬♪

steps.name: Percival
steps.text: The Victorian national anthem.

steps.name: Percival
steps.text: Our teacher made us sing it over and over until we had it memorized when I was little—before I got sick.

steps.name: Percival
steps.text: It's been a long time since I last heard it.

steps.name: Percival
steps.text: I was born in Victoria. By all accounts, I should be Victorian. But what about now?

steps.name: Guard
steps.text: That sergeant believed he belonged to Victoria to the very end.

steps.name: Percival
steps.text: He was lucky. He didn't get to go through... everything he would have gone through.

steps.name: Percival
steps.text: The reason I called myself Reunion—

steps.name: Percival
steps.text: I was tired of being punched, being thrown out of factories before I got paid, being kept out of even the cheapest hostel rooms, no matter how much money I had on me.

steps.name: Percival
steps.text: The Reunion Movement showed me another path, besides suffering and dying in silence. That was all I needed.

steps.name: Percival
steps.text: Even if the price was abandoning my family, my country, and everything else I had.

steps.name: Percival
steps.text: In fact, I had lost all of it the moment the first crystal popped through my skin. But it took me a long time to get it.

steps.name: Percival
steps.text: All of us, Ursine, Columbian, Victorian, Sarkaz, Feline, Liberi...

steps.name: Percival
steps.text: We are all Reunion.

steps.name: Guard
steps.text: If we have to cross every battlefront, every war zone, every corpse-laden ruin, in order for our deaths to be seen and heard...

steps.name: Guard
steps.text: Then we'll cross them.
